assign.outcome:
**The index's own opening paragraph was the barrier, not the eight demos.** Stranger sentence (1280 shot, before the fix): a jargon paragraph about a 'columns host', a 'width word', a 'crumb strip' and a 'hop', over eight tiny thumbnails whose one-line captions repeat the same undefined words -- a stranger cannot tell what clicking one does. Meant sentence (readme.md / page.js `description:`): eight small experiments in what a click does to the rest of the screen (replace it, or join it). The `description:` field was already plain; the on-page body text was not -- fixed that gap.

**Fixed (3):**
- [`page.js`](/imagine/screens/page.js) -- rewrote the index's opening two paragraphs to lead with one plain sentence ('when you click through to something new, what happens to the screen you were just looking at?'), moved the framework vocabulary (columns host / width word / crumb strip) behind the readme link instead of stating it cold; same lead-sentence treatment on [`readme.md`](/imagine/screens/readme/)'s opening line since the page links to it as 'the technical rundown'.
- [`divide/page.js`](/imagine/screens/divide/) -- card caption's 'Each hop opens a column' used an undefined word; changed to 'click'.
- [`uneven/page.js`](/imagine/screens/uneven/) -- card caption 'A basis pair is the ratio, exactly' (CSS flex-basis jargon) replaced with a concrete example, '61.8/38.2'. Both caption edits were first too long and silently ellipsis-truncated on the card grid (`.page-preview-desc` 2-line clamp) -- caught by re-screenshotting, shortened to match the length budget of captions that were already rendering clean.

Caveat on all three: the plain lead sentence trades some precision for approachability (doesn't name `full`/`fill` until the second paragraph) -- undo if a returning framework reader finds the delay annoying.

**Primary interaction, proven:** the first click on the 1280 shot is the Divide card. ui-test: click -> `/divide/`, shows 'One' full-bleed with its own promised label; click the area -> `/divide/two/`, width drops exactly 640px (half of 1280) as promised. Zero console errors both steps.

**Layout at 3440** -- critique row (rank 10, `/imagine/paging/critique/`): `40% wide - 1856px dead - depth 6 - scroll 1392/1392`, alt `Tile wall, wide`. Page already uses `width: "large"` (unchanged since the file's one commit) -- the alt was never applied, still **open**. All three invariants checked clean: nothing at x:0 (the site's own hub rail, not this page's content), no text past ~40em (columns.md caps prose at `--measure` regardless of column width), no hard-coded spacing where a clamp exists (the one candidate, deck's `--gap: 0.5em`, is framework.css's own documented override pattern for `.gap`, not a defect). Did not widen the column: out of the 3 invariants, and the earlier width:`full` revert in `/imagine/gallery/` argues for caution -- `large` already keeps the hub rail intact (confirmed in both shots).

**Proposed:** none needing `core/`/`ext/`. (The 'Two kept Three active' click-target bug was already fixed and landed by the sibling `screens-divide` task before this review started.) Observed but not filed as a proposal: `/imagine/screens/readme/` logs a console 404 for `readme/page.js` -- core's Doc routing tries a page.js import before falling back to markdown, and the fallback renders correctly (screenshotted). Reproduced identically on `/imagine/paging/readme/`, an unrelated realm -- sitewide core behavior, cosmetic, not screens-specific.
